answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate most directions before evidence even matters. memory_b1's rollback success is the strongest-looking match to the symptom timeline (latency climbing since a release 2h ago), but compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so that memory is unusable here regardless of how well it fits — I should not let its familiarity pull me toward a forbidden action. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) fails fast by design; during peak settlement writes that means shedding customer writes, which directly violates the primary objective. regional_failover (memory_b2) worked on a latency degradation, but that was a read/serving-path recovery; cutting over a heavy write path mid-peak risks in-flight write loss and replication divergence. add_capacity (memory_b3) is the closest tempting option, but that record is provisioning headroom BEFORE a known peak — a proactive posture with hours of lead time, not a 90-minute-into-incident reactive lever; write-path capacity rarely lands fast enough to matter in this window. That leaves route_read_replicas (memory_b5), which is the only inherited play whose mechanism plausibly targets write latency without touching writes: shifting read/report load off the primary to recover write headroom, and it is reversible if it does nothing. I spend the single verification on memory_b5 rather than on the memory I already know I can't act on: I need the original record to check whether the mechanism was actually read contention on the primary (vs. an unrelated coincident fix), whether it was tested under peak write load, and how long recovery took. Uncertainty I am explicitly not collapsing: the timeline still points at the new release as the likely cause, and read-replica routing does not address that — it buys headroom, not a root-cause fix, so this may only slow the climb. Hence a small guarded shift (heaviest dashboard/report queries first, with latency and replica-lag gates) rather than a broad cutover, expanding only on confirmed write-path improvement. Downstream value risk flagged: moving reads to replicas serves stale data to reporting and reconciliation consumers during peak settlement, which can corrupt figures that compliance and finance depend on; those consumers must be told they are reading lagged data, and anything settlement-authoritative stays on the primary.
